notes: Overturn confirmed. GR3 transfers the text to 'the receiving character positions of the area referenced by identifier-1'. When identifier-1 is a group holding its own ODO object, it is a receiving item, and 'the maximum length of the group will be used' (VI.5.8.4 GR3b). EmitReceive passes OperandText.RecordAreaImage(into), the image at the object's current value (CommunicationEmitter.cs line 93), so the runtime fills the current length. Rerun g2.cob: with GN=3 the 9-character message gives TEXT LENGTH 0004 and END KEY 0, and the rest comes back as a new message. Expected TEXT LENGTH 0009, END KEY 2. MOVE into the same group uses 10 positions (MV [9ABCDEFGH ]). The own probe separates the readings with a 4-character message at GN=1 (current length 2): observed 0002/0, expected 0004/2. Its control, with the ODO object outside the group (GR3a, current length), gives 0002 and is right. A side observation for the fix: after RECEIVE, the positions past the transferred text up to the group's maximum length come back as spaces, while the control (no RECEIVE) keeps them. With the area at its maximum length, GR3's 'without space fill' and GR8b's 'are not changed' cover those positions, so the fix's test must check them. The note PB5377 is right in its citations, its expected result ('position 10 unchanged') and its sites. kb/Work PB5377 holds the defect (adjudication: held-85/set5/decisions.json).

next.reason: 1985: "transferred to the receiving character positions of the area referenced by identifier-1 aligned to the left without space fill"; 2023: "Communication module (CD/MCS queues) dropped; new RECEIVE says only "The content of identifier-1 is the content of the message sent by that SEND statement"". The 2023 RECEIVE is a different run-unit messaging feature, not the 1985 CD-based statement, and it states no rule on left alignment or on omitting space fill.
